label: Something in this world is being moved; this is evident to the senses, from thought
meaning: Motion fork (#536): the Cogito trunk reaches a root-path premise. Take the occurring episode and its bearer (thinkingSubjectOfThought); by the open bridge STMT-COGITO-BORNE-THOUGHT-IS-OPINING the bearer opines the episode's content; by the open premise STMT-OPINION-IS-A-MOTION (Physics VIII.3, a reputable opinion) it is being moved in the respect of that opinion. Conclusion: the Lean content of STMT-SOMETHING-IS-MOVED-IN-THIS-WORLD, ∃ x r, MovedIn x r, in the broad sense of motion (DISAMB-MOTION). It does not give the statement's warrant ('evident to the senses'), a physical or local motion, motion in the world of sense, or concreteness and world-indexed existence of the moved thing; the Lean type of the premise does not encode 'in this world'. All four premises are open; STMT-OPINION-IS-A-MOTION is blocked by McTaggart's surviving rival (ATTEMPT-MCTAGGART-NOE-II-RETORSION-REPLY). Each premise is needed (COGITO-CONCRETE-OMISSION-CONTROLS). Reading: the route supports STMT-SOMETHING-IS-MOVED-IN-THIS-WORLD only on the broad sense DEF-MOTION-AS-REDUCTION, unless opinion-as-motion is itself read physically; DISAMB-MOTION's 'holds on either reading' rests on sense evidence, which this route does not supply. Passing from thought to opining is the explicit bridge of DISAMB-THOUGHT-VS-OPINING.
